note: Rejudged 2026-10-24 by an independent auditor (authored none of it). RFC 8654 Section 5, rfc/full/rfc8654.txt:171-176: "A BGP speaker that has the ability to use BGP Extended Messages but has not advertised the BGP Extended Message Capability, presumably due to configuration, MUST NOT accept a BGP Extended Message." STALE because 1dbfd1d7b7 changed capability.Negotiate: it now keeps the peer's Multiprotocol capabilities in OPEN order (remoteOrder) and builds familySlice from it, for ExaBGP's negotiated-family order. Read the whole diff: it touches only the Multiprotocol case, the implicit-family fallback and the family slice; the Extended Message handling, the per-direction receive limit and every other capability branch are unchanged, and negotiateWith is unchanged. The tagged carriers are byte-identical, so the earlier judgement stands: the receive limit follows the local OPEN, and a message over 4096 octets is refused when the local side did not advertise the capability, whatever the peer advertised. Separate from this verdict, the revert records for RFC8654-5-1 no longer verify (producer-changed) and owe re-recording; that is a discrimination-record violation, not a stale verdict.
